summary: Ryotai Shibuya was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tendai Sect University and Kokugakuin University.

Ryoun Yamada is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Harvard Business School. He worked at Mitsubishi Bank (~1964–1996), Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi (~1996–2000), Mitsubishi UFJ Securities, Tokyu Railways, and Itoki Corporation, and became Leiter at Sanbo Zen in 2004.

Ryudo Fujii is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Albrecht Wezler and Harunaga Isaacson. He held positions at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2003), Kokushikan University (attested 2010), and Kyoto Women's University (attested 2015).
Ryudo Suita is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 1997–2010) and was affiliated with Bukkyo University again (attested 2020).

Ryugen Taga is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1953–1955). He spent his academic career at Rissho University as lecturer (~1960–1968), associate professor (~1968–1976), professor (~1976–2002), and president (~1992–1995).

Ryugen Tanemura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held positions at Nishogakusha University (attested 2013), Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014), and Taisho University (attested 2014–2026).

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies, Abe studied at Keio, Johns Hopkins, SAIS, Taisho, and Columbia. He taught at Columbia (1991; 1998–2004) before becoming Reischauer Institute Professor of Japanese Religions at Harvard (~2006).

Ryujo Yamada was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied under Sylvain Lévi. He was a collaborator at Hōbōgirin and held posts at Tohoku University (professor attested 1953, emeritus 1972–1973) and Musashino University (attested 1963).

Ryuken Nawa is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar with attested 2026 lecturer posts at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Ryuken Sato was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an advisor at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute and professor emeritus at Taisho University (both attested 2014).
Ryuo was a Buddhist studies scholar who held teaching positions at To-ji and Koyasan University.
Ryusei Keira is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied under Tom Tillemans at the University of Lausanne, completing a thesis by 2003.
Ryushin Kitao is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Shuchiin University (attested 2014 and 2026).
Ryushin Saito is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. Saito served as a professor at Bukkyo University (attested 2015) and as faculty at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

Ryushin Sudo was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Taisho University (~1949–1953). He served as a lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Ryushin Uryuzu was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Ryukoku University. He held positions at the Tibetan Tripitaka Research Institute (attested 1962) and as professor at Kyoto Women's University (attested 1982).

Ryusho Hikata was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar educated at Tokyo and Tohoku universities. He taught at the University of Tokyo (1937), held professorships and a deanship at Kyushu University (1940–1958), and served as president of Fukuoka Women's University (1960–1964).

Ryuta Kikutani is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar. Kikutani held posts at Tohoku University (attested 2015), Kyoto University (attested 2020), and Koyasan University as associate professor (attested 2026).

Ryutaro Tsuchida is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Marburg, where he was later an assistant (~1980–1983). He became a professor at the University of Tokyo in 1983 (emeritus 1995–2012).

Takayoku Kimura is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Komazawa University. He served as research assistant at the University of Tokyo (~1973), lecturer at Yamaguchi University (attested 1996), and head priest at Kaichōji (attested 2003).
